title: Will the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee report more than $60M in cash on hand at the end of Q3? Above $60M
rules: If the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee's cash on hand is above $60 million as of September 30, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: This market resolves based on the official filing data released by the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Only the first official or non-preliminary release of the relevant statistic will be used to resolve the market, and subsequent revisions, corrections, or updates will not affect resolution.

blind.reasoning: The DCCC had $76M cash on hand at the end of August 2026, after falling about $4M in August while raising $12M. To land at or below $60M it would need to lose more than $16M net in September. That would take spending above about $30M, which is possible as fall ad spending ramps up but would be a big jump from August. End-of-quarter fundraising should partly offset the spending, so finishing above $60M is somewhat more likely than not.
blind.falsifier: The DCCC's September monthly FEC report (due around Oct 20, 2026) showing cash on hand at or below $60M, most likely because of heavy September independent-expenditure ad spending.

final.reasoning: The 16% price suggests traders expect very heavy September spending, so I've moved down a lot from 64%. Going from $76M to at or below $60M still takes more than $16M of net burn in one month, which I think the market is overpricing.
